title: Decouple build graph and add incremental CI checkpoints
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: our monolithic build graph and full-pipeline CI runs slow iteration and increase cost for PRs that touch a small subset of services. This PR separates the internal build dependency graph from CI orchestration, introduces per-package incremental checkpointing for test artifacts, and wires a lightweight detection layer to only run downstream stages when inputs changed. Goals: reduce PR feedback loop, lower CI minutes for typical infra/SDK changes, and make release hooks deterministic for incremental releases. What I changed (high level): decoupled core build graph (tools/build/graph.py) into an explicit dependency manifest and runtime loader; added incremental checkpoint producer/consumer (tools/build/checkpoint.py + scripts/ci/checkpoint-restore.sh); implemented a CI policy layer (ci/policies/detect-changes.py) that computes minimal stage sets; updated GitHub Actions workflows to support staged checkpoints and conditional jobs; documented the policy and rollback steps in docs/ci/README.md.

Implementation notes: the build graph is now a JSON manifest generated at build-time (tools/build/manifest_writer) and consumed by the CI runtime to compute subgraphs; checkpointing serializes test results and selected artifacts (hash keyed) to a short-lived S3-compatible store used by runners; restoration is best-effort and fails safe (if a checkpoint is missing we fall back to full stage). The CI policy uses a fast file-globbing change classifier with a small mapping table (repo paths -> stage names) and a conservative fallback to full CI for PRs with broad touches. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag (env CI_USE_CHECKPOINTS), run on canary repo subset for 48 hours, monitor false negatives (missed changes) and CI flakiness, then enable by default. Checklist: - [x] implement manifest writer and loader - [x] add checkpoint producer and consumer - [x] integrate with GitHub Actions and add conditional job gates - [x] document behavior and rollback steps - [x] smoke at scale on canary repos - [x] add metrics (ci.checkpoint.hit/miss, ci.stage.count) Additional context: this change is part of ENG-3176 to reduce median CI time for SDK/infra PRs by 40%. A separate follow-up will expose checkpoint telemetry in the Console and add heuristics to re-run flaky stages automatically.
commit_summary: feat(build): split build graph into manifest + loader; feat(ci): add incremental checkpoint producer/consumer; ci(workflows): conditional staged jobs using change detector; docs: add CI README and rollout notes; fix(tests): adapt unit tests to new manifest loader
small_snippets:
--- a/tools/build/checkpoint.py
+++ b/tools/build/checkpoint.py
@@ def restore_checkpoint(key):
-    # naive: always rebuild
-    return None
+    # try restore from store, return None on miss (caller does full build)
+    obj = store.get(key)
+    return obj if obj and verify(obj) else None
